briefdescription.para: Canonical seed used for all deterministic randomness in P6-03 tests.

xrefdescription.para: FI-01 Single participant partitioned during Phase-1 → coordinator aborts.

detaileddescription.para: Partition is established before Phase-1 begins. The partitioned participant cannot vote, so the coordinator receives a prepare failure and issues ABORT.

xrefdescription.para: FI-02 All participants partitioned during Phase-1 → coordinator aborts (no votes).
FI-03 Single participant partitioned after PREPARED (Phase-2 delivery fails) → re-drive delivers COMMIT once partition heals.
FI-04 Majority partitioned → abort decision; minority-only txn does not commit.
FI-05 Partition heals → pending COMMIT re-delivered idempotently.
FI-06 Network partition during 3PC PreCommit phase → fail-closed abort.
FI-07 Transient partition (appears + heals within same txn) → COMMIT succeeds.

detaileddescription.para: Partition is applied and healed before the coordinator sends any messages.

xrefdescription.para: FI-08 Cascading partition – participants fail one-by-one mid-prepare.

detaileddescription.para: Participants 0 and 1 succeed Phase-1; participant 2 is partitioned → abort.

xrefdescription.para: FI-09 Split-brain: two coordinator instances process the same txn_id → only one unique decision is stored in the WAL.

detaileddescription.para: Both coordinators share the same WAL. The second coordinator detects an existing COMMIT and does not append a second COMMIT/ABORT.

xrefdescription.para: FI-10 Partition during SAGA compensation step → compensate re-delivered.
FI-11 Coordinator isolated from all participants → times out + aborts.
FI-12 Participant isolated post-PREPARED; coordinator waits, then aborts on timeout.
FI-13 Percolator primary-lock write fails due to partition → txn aborts cleanly.
FI-14 Multiple concurrent partitioned txns – state isolation (no cross-contamination).
FI-15 Recovery after partition heals: WAL replay re-drives all in-doubt txns.
FI-16 Coordinator crash after PREPARE-sent, before COMMIT decision → participants in-doubt; recovery delivers COMMIT.
FI-17 Coordinator crash after ABORT decision logged but before delivery → recovery re-delivers ABORT.
FI-18 Coordinator restart with clean WAL → begins fresh; prior in-doubt txns recovered.

detaileddescription.para: Demonstrates that the new coordinator correctly identifies zero in-doubt txns when the WAL contains only a fully completed transaction.

xrefdescription.para: FI-19 New coordinator takes over → reads WAL, drives in-doubt txn to completion.
FI-20 Coordinator fails on every txn → each independently recoverable.
FI-21 Coordinator crash mid-3PC (after PreCommit sent, before Commit) → recovery re-drives COMMIT.
FI-22 WAL persists decision before coordinator crash → exactly-once delivery after recovery.
FI-23 Coordinator crash during SAGA execution → compensating actions re-driven from WAL.
FI-24 Multiple coordinator restarts on same in-doubt txn → idempotent recovery (same result each time).
FI-25 Concurrent txns; coordinator crashes during one; others complete normally.
FI-26 Two participants fail simultaneously during Phase-1 → coordinator aborts immediately.
FI-27 Cascade: Participant A fails → coordinator aborts → WAL records ABORT → Participant B receives ABORT via WAL replay.
FI-28 Three-way cascade: P1 votes yes, P2 partitioned, P3 timeout → atomic abort across all.
FI-29 Overlapping recovery: two in-doubt txns recovered simultaneously (concurrently).
FI-30 Stale lock cleanup: orphan locks held by crashed coordinator released after timeout.
FI-31 5-shard txn with 2 failures: deterministic abort regardless of failure order.
FI-32 SAGA multi-step: step 3 fails → compensate steps 2 and 1 in reverse order.
FI-33 Cascade with WAL gap: one WAL write fails → txn treated as in-doubt, recovers via participant probe.

detaileddescription.para: Simulated by not writing PREPARE to the WAL for one txn; the recovery engine cannot find it in-doubt so the txn is treated as lost/never-started.

xrefdescription.para: FI-34 Lock ordering: concurrent txns contending on same resources; deadlock-free via timeout.

detaileddescription.para: Two transactions each try to acquire two locks in the same order (consistent global ordering prevents deadlock). With consistent ordering only one succeeds.

xrefdescription.para: FI-35 Calvin deterministic ordering: second txn runs only after first commits.
FI-36 Percolator: primary-lock holder fails → new txn takes over via cleanup + re-lock.
FI-37 Replication lag simulation: participant commits but replica lags → read sees stale data until catch-up.
FI-38 Thundering herd recovery: 10 in-doubt txns all recovered concurrently.
FI-39 Durability proof: decision logged to WAL survives "restart" (WAL snapshot re-applied).
FI-40 End-to-end fault stress: random fault injection over 20 txns; verify no txn is both committed and aborted (consistency invariant).
